div.head: ECf 22
div.ab: Sochne: quod, si aliquis querit aliquid in terra sua, etiam furtum, sua est iusticia, si inuentum fuerit an non.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 647 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann’s upright (roman) letter a after “Sochne” refers to his explanatory notes, the Erklärungen (printed as Gesetze III; his note on p. 627 calls it “Band II”), which are not yet added here.

note.seg: ohne dass (wie in 22, 1) der Beklagte sofort benannt wäre, z. B. in Spurfolge
without the defendant being named at once (as in 22, 1), e.g. in tracking
dann also nicht handhaftes Verbrechen, im Gegensatz zu infangene-þeof 22, 4
so then not a crime caught in the act, in contrast to infangene-þeof, 22, 4
so S Ad Wo, die est zufügen; Sooc Hr; Socha übr.; dieser Satz steht in Ad Do Wo Retr. hinter 22, 1
so S Ad Wo, which add est; Sooc Hr; Socha the others; in Ad Do Wo and the Retr. this sentence stands after 22, 1

div.ab: Soke (Sochne): that, if anyone searches for anything in his land, even for theft, the justice is his, whether it has been found or not.
